recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant source prose for the removed elements; future mentions should remain limited to migration or compatibility guidance unless the work group makes a new decision.
issue_request: FHIR-29034 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request for R5 asking to remove top-level Organization.telecom and Organization.address and update Organization.contact from a BackboneElement to 0..* ExtendedContactDetail.
initial_application: The change was applied in stages: a9d7aa77 changed Organization.contact to ExtendedContactDetail while temporarily deprecating top-level telecom/address; e1320848 removed those deprecated Organization.telecom and Organization.address elements from the active StructureDefinition; eb428f54 retargeted Organization address search parameters to Organization.contact.address.
additional_context: FHIR-29035 created ExtendedContactDetail, and FHIR-27005 records that using ExtendedContactDetail on Organization.contact satisfies the missing contact period request. PA 2021-12-01 minutes confirm the decision. Remaining Organization.telecom/address mentions are compatibility mappings in source/fhir.ini [r4-r6-changes] or in an inactive commented CDA profile, not active Organization elements.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Source inspection confirmed Organization is active, Organization.contact is typed as ExtendedContactDetail, Organization.telecom/address element definitions are absent, Organization address search parameters use Organization.contact.address, and active Organization examples do not contain direct root telecom/address children.

related_jiras.note: Location.contact followed the same ExtendedContactDetail migration pattern and was part of the originating PA discussion, but it is a separate Location issue and was not decided here.
Created the ExtendedContactDetail datatype that Organization.contact now uses.
Its Organization contact period request is satisfied by Organization.contact using ExtendedContactDetail.
